narrative.overview:
Sahaj Atlas is a bright, sunny map with a white panel beside it (a bottom sheet on a phone). It belongs to the We Meditate family and lives inside other people's websites, so it has to feel welcoming without taking over the page. The warmth comes from colour, never from decoration: sand neutrals instead of blue-grey, green map markers, and one coral accent, on plain white panels. The interface is quiet so that the one answer a seeker came for (when and where can I go) stands out.

Density is calm and list-shaped. Every panel row shares one 24px edge and one row height, text sits on one short type ladder, and the search field is the first thing under the title. Dark mode follows the device and keeps the same warmth: a sand-dark ramp and a warm taupe basemap instead of the stock blue-black.

The approved round-2 look rejected, by name: gradients and washes (a watercolour header was withdrawn), a greyed "quiet" map, dark-teal or high-contrast cluster markers, a single flattened chip style, and a set of decorative We Meditate icons.
keyCharacteristics: Bright, sunny light basemap; warm taupe dark basemap.
Green pins and clusters with white counts; coral marks the chosen class.
One decorative icon in the whole interface: the We Meditate meditating figure.
Search first: the place search sits at the top of the home panel, under the title.
Host brand colours repaint every brand role, so meaning never depends on one fixed hue.

rules.name: The Warm-Through-Colour Rule
rules.body: Warmth comes from the sand neutrals, the green markers and the coral accent. Never from gradients, washes, textures or ornament.

rules.name: The Repaint Rule
rules.body: Primary, secondary and contrast are host roles and repaint at runtime. Never let a state or meaning depend on one of them alone; pair colour with text, weight or shape.

rules.name: The Coral Is Rare Rule
rules.body: Coral marks the chosen class on the map, the "today" tag and the meditating figure. Nothing else.

rules.name: The One Ladder Rule
rules.body: Sizes are 12, 14, 15, 16 and 20px, all in px (a host's root font size must not rescale the widget). No tracking on body text.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: Inputs render at 16px on touch screens so iOS never zooms the host page; 14px only with a wide screen and a fine pointer.

rules.name: The One Edge Rule
rules.body: Nothing in a panel invents its own inset. If a row does not start at 16px, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Float Over The Map Rule
rules.body: Shadows exist to lift a surface off the map. A card inside a panel never gets one.

rules.name: The Two Corners Rule
rules.body: 16px for a surface on the map, 8px for anything on that surface, round only for pills. No 2, 4 or 6px corners.

dos: **Do** take every neutral from the sand ramp through the `gray-*` names, and every brand colour from the role ramps, so hosts can repaint them.
**Do** keep every panel row on the 16px gutter and the 56px row height.
**Do** use the type ladder (12, 14, 15, 16, 20px) in px, with sentence-case copy and uppercase only through CSS.
**Do** keep the search field first on the home panel, under the title.
**Do** keep the light basemap bright and sunny, and apply the warm paint to the dark one.
**Do** keep coral for the selected class, the today tag and the meditating figure.
**Do** hold 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for icons and large text, on both the warm white and the night panel.
donts: **Don't** use gradients, washes, watercolour, textures or decorative illustration.
**Don't** add decorative icons. The meditating figure on the online row is the only one; the near-me row has no icon.
**Don't** grey out the map or recolour clusters dark teal.
**Don't** flatten the tags into one neutral style; each keeps its tinted role colour.
**Don't** tint a notice coral or red. A passive note, like the location guess, sits on the sand-3 fill so it never reads as an error.
**Don't** use corners other than 16px, 8px and fully round.
**Don't** put a group label above a title or heading; it names a group of rows, nothing else.
**Don't** use rem units; a host's root font size would rescale the widget.
